summary.text: Palynology is the study of tiny acid-resistant organic remains, such as pollen and spores, found in sediments and sedimentary rocks.
Fossil pollen and other palynomorphs show what kind of life existed when each layer was laid down, which gives clues to past environments and climates.
Quantitative pollen analysis began with Lennart von Post, and after Gunnar Erdtman's 1921 thesis the method spread across Europe and North America and transformed Quaternary climate research.

facts.label: Abundance
facts.value: Millions per gram in organic marine deposits

items.prompt: A lab dissolves a mud sample in strong acid to strip away the minerals. Why are the pollen grains still there afterwards?

options.label: They sink before the acid reaches them
They are made of hard mineral crystal
Their organic walls resist the acid
The acid is too weak to dissolve anything

items.explain: Palynomorphs are made of acid-resistant organic material, so acid digestion removes the non-organic part and leaves them behind.

items.prompt: A jar sold as local mountain honey is suspected of being fake. How could pollen help check it?

options.label: Pollen in it shows its plant and place sources
Pollen makes real honey taste sweeter
Fake honey has more pollen than real honey
Pollen reveals the date the jar was sealed

items.explain: Studying pollen in honey identifies its sources by location and plant genus, a tool for catching adulterated and mislabeled honey.

items.prompt: Detectives want to show a suspect's boots were at a particular field. How could palynology help?

options.label: By dating the leather of the boots
By measuring the wear on the soles
By testing the boots for fingerprints
By matching microscopic grains on them

items.explain: Forensic palynology uses palynomorphs as evidence to prove or disprove a physical link between objects, people and places.

items.prompt: A geologist hunts for ancient pollen in rock that was later heated and recrystallized deep underground. What should she expect?

options.label: Pollen preserved better than usual
Pollen generally destroyed
Pollen turned into living spores
Pollen grown larger than normal

items.explain: Palynomorphs have generally been destroyed in metamorphic or recrystallized rocks.

items.prompt: In a lake bed, one layer is full of pollen from one set of plants and a deeper layer from very different plants. What does this most likely show?

options.label: Pollen sinks at different speeds
The deeper layer formed more recently
Plant life and climate changed over time
Pollen moved between the two layers

items.explain: Palynomorphs record the kind of life present when each layer was laid down, so a change in pollen points to a change in conditions, including climate.

items.prompt: A scientist studies diatoms, tiny organisms with glassy silica shells, in lake mud. Does that count as palynology?

options.label: No, shelled organisms like these are excluded
Yes, all microfossils in mud count
Yes, as long as they are in sediment
Only if they are under 500 micrometres

items.explain: Palynology does not include diatoms, foraminiferans or other organisms with siliceous or calcareous tests.
